findings.note: The question as served says the plane makes 60 deg with the horizontal; the solution solves for 30 deg, a value the question text does not give. For 60 deg, mu = tan60 = sqrt(3) = 1.73. My answer differs from the solution's.

findings.fix: The question text gives 60 deg (the figure description says 30 deg; the text is followed here). Put in θ = 60°: μ = tan60° = √3 ≈ 1.73.

findings.quote: At 30 degrees, tan gives the exact ratio of the sliding force to the holding force, independent of the particle's mass.
findings.note: At the point of slipping the holding force (friction) equals the sliding force, so their ratio is 1, not tan(theta). tan(theta) is the ratio of the weight's along-slope component to the normal force, and equals mu only at limiting friction. Also cites 30 deg where the question gives 60 deg.
findings.fix: tan(theta) is the ratio of the weight's component along the slope, mg sin(theta), to the normal force, mg cos(theta); at the point of slipping the limiting friction mu N equals mg sin(theta), so this ratio is mu, whatever the particle's mass.

findings.quote: The mass mg cancels from both sides, leaving a relation that depends only on the angle.
findings.note: mg is the weight, not the mass.
findings.fix: The common factor mg cancels from both sides, leaving a relation that depends only on the angle.
